text: Andrea Carol Arpaci-Dusseau (also published as Andrea Dusseau) is an American computer scientist specializing in operating systems, file systems, data storage, distributed computing, and computer science education. She is a professor of computer sciences at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Along with her husband, Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, she co-authored the free 2018 textbook "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP), which is downloaded millions of times annually and is used at hundreds of institutions worldwide. Arpaci-Dusseau earned her bachelor's degree in computer engineering from Carnegie Mellon University, graduating in 1991, and completed her Ph.D. in computer science at the University of California, Berkeley in 1998; her dissertation, "Implicit Coscheduling: Coordinated Scheduling with Implicit Information in Distributed Systems," was supervised by David Culler. After conducting postdoctoral research at Stanford University, she joined the University of Wisconsin–Madison faculty as an assistant professor in 2000 and became a full professor in 2009. She primarily teaches undergraduate and graduate-level operating systems courses. Arpaci-Dusseau is married to Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, who is also a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison and an expert in data storage; the two are frequent collaborators. In 2018, Arpaci-Dusseau and her husband received the SIGOPS Mark Weiser Award "for outstanding leadership, innovation, and impact in storage and computer systems research." She was named an ACM Fellow in 2020 "for contributions to storage and computer systems."
